statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) such that len(r) = 2, r[0] and r[1] are No-Zero integers, and r[0] + r[1] = n.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000 (10^4). A No-Zero integer is a positive integer whose standard base-10 representation (without leading zeros) contains no digit 0; equivalently, x > 0 and for every integer k with 0 <= k and 10^k <= x, floor(x / 10^k) mod 10 != 0. The problem guarantees that at least one pair of No-Zero integers sums to n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = 2.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 <= r[0] <= n - 1 and 1 <= r[1] <= n - 1.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000.

statement: The function returns a result r for every such n; in particular, evaluation does not fail with arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000; the problem guarantees a valid No-Zero decomposition exists.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r[0] is a No-Zero integer, i.e. r[0] > 0 and every decimal digit in the standard base-10 representation of r[0] is nonzero.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r[1] is a No-Zero integer, i.e. r[1] > 0 and every decimal digit in the standard base-10 representation of r[1] is nonzero.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r[0] + r[1] = n.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r[0] > 0 and r[1] > 0.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer k with 0 <= k and 10^k <= r[0], the k-th decimal digit of r[0], namely floor(r[0] / 10^k) mod 10, is nonzero.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer k with 0 <= k and 10^k <= r[1], the k-th decimal digit of r[1], namely floor(r[1] / 10^k) mod 10, is nonzero.
preconditions: n is an integer with 2 <= n <= 10000.
